newsitem.title: USA: Perot low key on presidential election prospects.
newsitem.headline: Perot low key on presidential election prospects.

text.p: Reform Party presidential candidate Ross Perot was low-key about his prospects in the presidential election on Tuesday but senior aides said they expected him to score a major upset.

Perot, who is stuck in single figures in most opinion polls, refused to offer a prediction on the election as he voted in his home town of Dallas in the morning. "We'll see how it works out," he told reporters before urging people to go to the polls and "vote their conscience."

Accompanied by his wife Margot and daughter Katherine, the self-made Texas billionaire said he would comment on his future plans on Tuesday night, but said he felt "great" and had enjoyed the campaign.
"Never dull. Always something going on," he said.

Perot's spokeswoman Sharon Holman said the Reform Party was confident Perot and his running mate Pat Choate would prove all the opinion polls wrong. "We are elated, delighted. We really believe we are going to surprise everyone tonight," she said. "There's going to be a big surprise, a major upset."

Holman said the party hoped to win at least 25 percent of the vote, qualifying it as a major party and guaranteeing it would receive federal funds equal to those given to the Republicans and Democrats in the next presidential election.
Perot won 19 percent of the popular vote in his independent bid for the White House in 1992 but he has drawn much less public interest this year.

In the last days of the campaign, he launched blistering attacks on President Bill Clinton's integrity, claiming that another four-year term would see criminal charges brought against Clinton and plunge the country into crisis.

"We are on the verge of Watergate II and a constitutional crisis ... Why would you even think about voting for a president who violates the law, doesn't tell the truth and doesn't keep his promises?" Perot said.
